chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: How the community regarded musicians
summary: Blakeney says musicians were thought of as loud and unprofessional, though some were respected as family men.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, would you state for us, if you can recall, the attitude of the community towards the musician at that time; how was the musician looked upon by the non-professionals in the community?
Not so good. He was considered loud and unprofessional.
What was the level of respect for them in the community? Were they considered as professionals?
Yes, in some ways. Some of the musicians were.
I guess as today some were respected more than others?
Some of those musicians were family men, with families, and were good family men.
